problems.statement: The 12-hour shift pattern (fatigue in late-shift hours) is the main cause of the yield decline, as the Plant Manager believes.

Deferred quarterly spindle service has left spindle bearings worn (runout above the 5 um limit, rising vibration on L3-02), degrading journal size and finish, especially on the tight-tolerance long-shaft machines L3-02 and L3-05.
The Corvane bar, with its widening within-lot hardness scatter after the 1 September billet source change, causes tool deflection and size/chatter rejects, and is a contributor to the decline.

The decline results from several overlapping Line 3 changes (spindle service deferral, steel change, 12-hour running, more offset keying) that cannot be separated with current data, because all of them changed at about the same time and the defect codes cannot tell them apart.
Undertrained new operators drive the decline.
The CMM or inspection system has drifted or become stricter, so the yield fall is a measurement artefact.
Operator fatigue is visible in the timing of scrap tags in the last hours of the shift.
Hand-keyed wear-offset errors, made more frequent by more insert changes, add to the size scatter.
The Line 3 problem is real and customer-visible, not just an internal reporting issue.

causalClaims.from: scrap tag timestamps late in shift

causalClaims.to: spindle wear and rising runout and vibration
journal size and chatter rejects, especially on L3-02 and L3-05

causalClaims.from: increased running hours (168 vs 120 per week)

actions.action: Do the deferred spindle service on L3-02 and L3-05 first, then the other four lathes, two at a time on weekend shifts, and set up a runout log with a no-skip rule.
actions.rationale: The Halvard backlog is down to 1.2 weeks and the buyer has agreed to a slower ship schedule, so service is cheap, low risk and overdue whichever explanation proves right.

actions.action: Pull the CMM results for the 1,400 long shafts made on Line 6 (serviced spindle, 8-hour shifts, Corvane bar) and compare them with Line 3 long-shaft results.
actions.rationale: This is nearly free and tests the steel against the worn-spindle explanation.

actions.action: Run Tamsworth trial lots on a serviced Line 3 spindle, ideally as a staged design that separates steel from spindle condition, and start matching lathe cycle-counter logs to CMM serials.
actions.rationale: It separates the steel and spindle effects, using the supplier's offer of trial lots within 10 days and the 180-day cycle-counter logs.

actions.action: Return Line 3 to 8-hour shifts from Monday as the fix.
actions.rationale: The evidence does not support fatigue as the cause, and the change would also confound the spindle and steel tests, though a later pattern change on other grounds such as fatigue is a separate decision.

actions.action: Cut final CMM inspection from 100% to 1-in-10 sampling and adopt Corvane permanently.
actions.rationale: The cause is unresolved, the customer is already rejecting parts, and sampling would let more defects reach Halvard and hide the signal while the root cause is unknown.

actions.action: Submit a containment and root-cause plan to Halvard by 13 November that keeps 100% inspection and includes a Corvane hardness-sorting or tighter hardness-spread requirement.
actions.rationale: It meets the customer deadline and protects shipments while the cause is being resolved.

actions.action: Retrain or discipline the new operators.
actions.rationale: The new operators' reject rates match those of experienced operators and the decline began before they ran machines alone.

actions.action: Add direct monitoring of the other spindles and record offset entries.
actions.rationale: L3-02 is the only lathe with a permanent sensor, and offset keying cannot currently be told apart from other causes.

nextEvidence: CMM results for the roughly 1,400 long shafts run on Line 6 (serviced spindle, Corvane bar, 8-hour shifts), compared with the L3-02 and L3-05 long-shaft results

Matching of the lathe cycle-counter logs to CMM serials, to give reject rate by machine, hour of cut and tool-change interval, plus before and after rates for L3-02 and L3-05 around the spindle service
A trial of Tamsworth lots on a freshly serviced Line 3 spindle, and Corvane bar on a freshly serviced spindle, to separate the steel and spindle effects
output.summary: The Plant Manager's fatigue-and-12-hour-shift explanation is not supported. Scrap tags are written in batches at shift end, so their times say nothing about when parts were cut. The decline began in week 32, before the new operators ran alone, and their reject rates match those of experienced operators. The CMM is stable. Two candidate causes remain, and the data cannot separate them: deferred spindle service (runout above limit, worsening vibration on L3-02) and wider hardness scatter in Corvane bar. Service the spindles now, pull the Line 6 results, and trial Tamsworth bar on a serviced spindle. Do not reduce inspection, and do not present the shift change as the fix.
